target.title: Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar exposes excellent provider-level usage details, but Settings has no single place to answer three basic cross-provider questions: **what did I spend, where did it go, and which models did I actually use?** This PR proposes one local, spend-first overview for that job.

The information hierarchy is deliberate:

1. aggregate estimated spend and tracked tokens;
2. ranked enabled subscriptions;
3. a separate ranked model list;
4. daily spend context;
5. local-data provenance and the existing cost-tracking control.

Alternatives considered:

- **Add totals to each provider pane:** reuses existing navigation but still cannot compare providers or models in one view.
- **Put the dashboard in the status menu:** makes a large analytical surface compete with the fast-glance quota workflow.
- **Reuse a web dashboard:** inconsistent coverage and privacy characteristics; the required local history already exists in `UsageStore`.

## What this adds

- A top-level **Usage & Spend** Settings destination with 7- and 30-day windows.
- Combined estimated spend, tracked tokens, subscription count, and priced-history coverage.
- Ranked subscription rows using existing provider icons/colors, model names, relative bars, tokens, and spend.
- A distinct model ranking built from real `modelBreakdowns`.
- A secondary daily spend chart and honest empty/unpriced states.
- Strict-locale strings and persisted Settings selection coverage.

## Data semantics

| Surface | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Estimated spend | Sum of finite, locally derived priced history in the selected window. |
| Tracked tokens | Sum of known local token history; missing history is not coerced to zero. |
| Subscription ranking | Spend first, then tracked tokens, then stable provider order. Rank compares local activity, not provider quality. |
| Model ranking | Aggregated per provider/model from actual daily model breakdowns. |
| Priced coverage | Count of enabled providers with priced history, shown alongside total enabled providers. |
| Daily chart | Existing local provider history bucketed by calendar day; no new collection or persistence. |

No upload, public link, backend, credential access, prompt capture, or account identity is introduced. Providers without priced history remain visible with `Spend unavailable` and do not dilute known totals.

## Relationship to sharing

- Companion draft: [#2112 — Add shareable subscription usage cards](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2112)
- This PR owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- #2112 owns fixed-image/text export only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime; the split preserves one concern per PR and allows independent product decisions.

## Why a dedicated pane

This is intentionally a draft because the dedicated top-level destination is a product decision, not an implementation inevitability. A separate pane avoids overloading provider settings or the menu, provides enough width for aligned comparisons, and keeps trend analysis out of the fast-glance path. If maintainers prefer a narrower overview inside an existing surface, the aggregation model can survive while the presentation is relocated.

## Verification

- [x] `swift build`
- [x] `swift test --filter UnifiedSpendDashboardModelTests` — 2 tests pass
- [x] `make check`
- [x] Local SwiftUI render with mixed priced/unpriced real aggregate history
- [ ] Sanitized screenshots for light/dark, 7/30-day, mixed-history, and empty states
- [ ] Full sharded suite in CI

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. This draft asks whether CodexBar should have a permanent, top-level spend-first dashboard, or whether the aggregate model should be presented inside an existing overview. It should remain a draft until maintainers choose that direction and inspect sanitized runtime proof.
